context: The item is a second-hand phone, recently serviced.
transcript: Buyer ($60): Hello! I am very interested in purchasing the recently serviced phone you have listed. Would you be willing to accept $60 for it?

Seller ($180): Hi there! Thanks for your interest, but $60 is unfortunately too low considering the phone was recently serviced and works like new. I would love to make a fair deal, so I can lower my asking price from $200 down to $180 for you.
Buyer ($105): Thank you for the counteroffer and for meeting me partway. I understand the value of a recently serviced phone, so I can increase my offer to $105. Would that work for you?

Seller ($160): I really appreciate you raising your offer to $105! However, given the recent servicing ensures the phone is in excellent working condition, $105 is still a bit too low. I can meet you further down at $160 for a fair deal.

Buyer ($135): Thank you for bringing the price down to $160. I can stretch my budget and raise my offer to $135, which is very close to my limit. Would you be willing to accept $135 so we can close the deal today?

Seller ($150): I really appreciate you stretching your budget to $135! However, $150 is the absolute lowest I can go to cover the recent servicing costs and ensure a fair deal for both of us. If you can meet me at $150, we can close the deal today!
Buyer ($150): That sounds completely fair, and I really appreciate you meeting me at $150. I am happy to accept this price and close the deal today. <AGREEMENT>
